bull_case: High recurring OCF allows Visa to keep investing and returning capital through downturns.
bear_case: A severe regulatory settlement plus global spending shock could reduce flexibility, but not plausibly force financing under current conditions.
thesis: Visa's balance sheet is easily supportable by cash generation. Net debt is modest relative to annual OCF and regulatory/litigation cash needs are manageable within internal liquidity.

evidence.claim: Q3 cash+investments were about $13.94B versus debt $23.86B.

counterevidence: Regulatory and interchange litigation can pressure network economics and pricing over time.
The current valuation already embeds a high-quality compounder profile.
unknowns: Long-run regulation of interchange and routing
Sustainable growth rate of Visa Direct and value-added services
falsifiers: If processed transactions and payments volume decelerate materially while client incentives rise faster than gross revenue, the moat/FCF thesis weakens.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Cash generation is sufficient; Visa is not structurally dependent on external capital.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 파산 또는 영구손실 확률이 기대수익에 비해 지나치게 높음
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Debt is small relative to OCF and the business has no credible near-term solvency pathway.

next_checks: Payments volume, cross-border volume, processed transactions, value-added services, client incentives, owner FCF/share, buyback price

subscores.rationale: Visa has modest net debt relative to enormous OCF, with diversified maturities and investment-grade access.
FY2025 OCF exceeded $23B and the business can fund capex, dividends and buybacks internally.
Shares are repurchased aggressively and SBC is modest; no off-balance obligation dominates the capital structure.

uncertainties.rationale: Regulation, incentives and valuation are the main uncertainty.
